scenes.title: Where and when
narration: Paiki developed from the military drills and traditions of the paik, the medieval foot soldiers of eastern central India.
It is historically associated with the Rautia, who served as soldiers during the reign of the Nagvanshi dynasty in the Chotanagpur plateau.
Over time, the martial practices of these foot soldiers evolved into a ceremonial dance tradition practiced across Jharkhand, Chhattisgarh, and Odisha.

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: Paiki is primarily performed at weddings and public or community functions.
Its core expressive meaning centers on the reflection and celebration of historical military valour.
Today it is a living tradition.

scenes.title: Listen
narration: The musical accompaniment is powered by four primary traditional instruments: the nagara drum, the large dhak drum, the melodic shehnai, and the narsingh horn.
Together they create an energetic acoustic framework that paces the dancers' martial steps.
Listen for the Nagara, Dhak, Shehnai, Narsingh.
The sonic landscape is defined by the resonant, thunderous strikes of nagara and dhak drums, pierced by the high melodic reed tones of the shehnai and the brass calls of the narsingh horn.

music_brief.sound_description: The sonic landscape is defined by the resonant, thunderous strikes of nagara and dhak drums, pierced by the high melodic reed tones of the shehnai and the brass calls of the narsingh horn.
music_brief.prompt: Original instrumental composition in the musical world of Paiki dance (India). Instruments: Nagara, Dhak, Shehnai, Narsingh. Mood: martial, valiant, celebratory, energetic. It should sound like this: The sonic landscape is defined by the resonant, thunderous strikes of nagara and dhak drums, pierced by the high melodic reed tones of the shehnai and the brass calls of the narsingh horn. New melody, new arrangement: do not quote or imitate any specific recorded song; keep the idiom, the instruments, the pulse and the proportions.

tracks.use: chapters: dance it to the music

rules: Original composition only — no sampling, no melody of any existing recording, no lyrics from any song.

Label every generated track with the tool, the date and this brief, so provenance is always clear.
